title: Enterprise Beta — Customer Savings Model v2
content:
Purpose
---
Quick, customer-specific savings analysis for Enterprise Beta (internal name: EB-42). The goal is to produce a before/after cost model tied to our Redwood Optimize recommendations so Sales and Solutions can present an expected monthly savings range and a conservative ROI timeline. This is a working doc — numbers come from customer billing export (Jan 2026) + quick profiling runs.

Customer snapshot
- Customer name: Enterprise Beta (EB-42) — B2B SaaS, single region (us-west1) production traffic
- Current infra: managed endpoints on cloud provider (p3-equivalent), mix of 8k and 16k token sequences, primarily for chat and generation routes
- Current monthly spend (inference only): $142,500 (billing export, Jan 2026)
- Peak concurrent requests: ~260
- Current SLA target: p95 latency < 1.4s

Data sources and assumptions
- Billing export processed: billing-2026-01.csv (imported into linked spreadsheet)
- Sampled 10k requests from production traces to estimate token distribution and seq length percentiles
- Model currently deployed: osp-m-70b-fp16 (baseline)
- Serving configuration: batch size 1–4 dynamic, no prefix caching, no quantized runtime
- Measurement window: 30 days (Jan 2026), normalized to 730 hours/month where appropriate
- Cost units: USD, inference-only (excludes data transfer and storage)

Methodology
- Baseline cost model: compute cost per token derived from billing and token counts. We use per-call overhead + per-token compute cost decomposition observed in trace profiling.
- Redwood Optimize recommendations considered: (1) Switch to osp-m-70b-quant-8 (8-bit) runtime variant, (2) enable prefix KV caching for chat sessions (expect 35–55% token savings on repeat turns), (3) conservative batching (increase effective batch window from 5ms to 15ms where p95 unaffected), (4) request routing to cheaper-compatible model for long sequences when quality acceptable (osp-m-70b-int8-faster).
- Conservative vs optimistic scenarios computed by varying cache hit and batching impact.

Key baseline metrics (derived)
- Monthly tokens (input+output): 1.8B tokens
- Avg tokens per request: 1,230
- Avg tokens per second (sustained): 695
- Baseline per-token compute cost (in practice): $0.000079 per token (inference cost only)
- Baseline effective per-request overhead (network + orchestration): $0.0065

Before / After summary (monthly)
- Baseline monthly cost: $142,500 (matches billing export after small smoothing)

ASCII table: baseline vs recommended (conservative / optimistic)
| Scenario       | Tokens (B) | Per-token $ | Total compute $ | Overhead $ | Total $    | Savings $ | Savings % |
|----------------|------------|-------------|-----------------|-----------:|-----------:|---------:|---------:|
| Baseline       | 1.80       | 0.000079    | 142,200         | 300        | 142,500    | 0        | 0%      |
| Conservative   | 1.17       | 0.000061    | 71,370          | 240        | 71,610     | 70,890   | 49.7%   |
| Optimistic     | 0.81       | 0.000049    | 39,690          | 180        | 39,870     | 102,630  | 72.0%   |
Notes on table calculations:
- Conservative scenario assumptions: cache hit 35% of output tokens for multi-turn chat, batching reduces effective per-token time by 22%, quantization yields 23% per-token compute reduction relative to fp16 when accounting for kernel mix and seq distribution, and selective routing moves 8% of long sequences to faster int8 path.
- Optimistic scenario assumptions: cache hit 55%, batching reduces time by 40%, quantization and kernel optimizations yield 38% per-token compute reduction, 15% of requests eligible for cheaper model.
- Overhead line item is scaled down proportional to total requests (we expect fewer token generations and slightly higher batching efficiency so orchestration overhead per month drops).

Sensitivity analysis (key drivers)
1) Cache hit rate on repeat turns
   - 20% hit -> ~33% savings
   - 35% hit -> ~50% savings (central estimate)
   - 55% hit -> ~68% savings
2) Batching latency allowance (affects p95)
   - If product refuses >10ms added queuing at p95, effective batching improvement limited to ~18% -> reduces projected savings by ~8–10 p.p.
3) Fraction of traffic convertible to cheaper model
   - Each additional 5% of traffic moved to int8-faster yields ~3% incremental total cost reduction

Short model-level breakdown (monthly compute $)
- osp-m-70b-fp16 (current): $93,000 (65% of compute cost)
- Background smaller models (rerankers, safety, prompt prep): $12,600 (9%)
- Token generation main path: $36,600 (26%)
After recommendations we expect quantized main path to drop to ~$27k (optimistic) or ~$61k (conservative) depending on adoption of cache & batching.

Risk / open questions
- Quality delta for long-form generation when using int8-faster variant — need eval set A/B with customer prompts (assigned to Priya).
- Customer product team may be unwilling to accept >10ms added p95 latency for some routes (work with SRE and product to identify routes that are latency-tolerant).
- Billing mismatch rounding: vendor invoice includes GPU-hour minimums; verify with finance that backend costs align with our per-token normalization (Evan to confirm).
- Security/compliance constraints for private deployment (if customer requires on-prem, model switching may be limited).

Actionable next steps (short horizon)
- Run 48h profile with Redwood Optimize agent enabled (non-prod) to measure real cache hit distribution and batching impact: assignee Jorge, ETA 2026-03-09.
- Create 2 evaluation prompts sets (chat and long-gen) and run quality regressions between fp16 and int8-faster: assignee Priya, ETA 2026-03-08.
- Update canonical spreadsheet with live profiling numbers and produce final proposal doc for AE: target date 2026-03-12 (link in linked_artifacts).

Appendix: quick calculations and formulas used
- per-token compute $ = total_compute_bill / monthly_tokens
- projected_tokens_after_cache = monthly_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_fraction * avg_cached_token_fraction)
- projected_compute_cost = projected_tokens_after_cache * per-token-quantized-rate * quantization_multiplier (applied per kernel mix)
- Simplified ROI: (Baseline - Projected)/Baseline and payback months = Implementation effort cost / monthly savings (implementation effort cost estimate: $7k for rollout and testing).

Notes to self (raw)
- Customer has heavy weekend batch usage; caching may be less effective on ad-hoc support chats — flag in pitch.
- Keep conservative numbers in AE deck; show optimistic as engineering upside.
- Consider offering a 3-month pilot pricing guarantee split 50/50 on measured savings to reduce customer risk.
